description: WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK03 at :324 - the FIRST arm of the main EVALUATE TRUE at :323-383 - reached with a BLANK caller context, and this folder's proof of the other half of gate G40: both fallbacks at :328-339 take their TRUE branch, so the XCTL target defaults to the main menu rather than to a caller. case15 pins the populated half with the same key, and the two differ only in the two CDEMO-FROM- fields that arrive and in the CDEMO-TO- pair and nextProgram that result. EIBAID is DFHPF3, which app/cpy/CSSTRPFY.cpy:34-35 - the seventh of that copybook's twenty-eight ordered arms, and one of the two that reach CCARD-AID-PFK03 since :58-59 folds PF15 onto it - stores as CCARD-AID-PFK03; PFK03 is one of only two AIDs the gate at :306-314 accepts, so it is not rewritten to ENTER, and because its arm is tested before both context arms it wins even though CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives as 1 (gate G30). The blank from-pair is arranged deliberately and the choice matters: the two fields are supplied as SPACES inside an otherwise fully populated commarea, with EIBCALEN 172 and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 1, rather than by passing EIBCALEN 0 and letting :285-286 INITIALIZE the area. Both routes reach the fallback, and the guard at :282-284 is ruled out twice over here: EIBCALEN is 172, which is CARDDEMO-COMMAREA's 160 bytes followed by WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA's 12, and eight spaces are not LIT-MENUPGM, so the AND fails on its first conjunct and again on NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER. Supplying the blank fields directly is preferred for three reasons: case01 already pins the EIBCALEN-zero initialise, so conflating the two would leave a reader unable to say which of them produced the CM00 target; the initialise would also blank the eight identity-bearing fields, weakening the statelessness assertion from real data surviving the turn to an initialised area coming back initialised (gate G37); and it is only COACTVWC's own guard that is being kept out of the way, never the fallback being tested. SPACES rather than LOW-VALUES is deliberate too: :328-329 and :334-335 are ordered disjunctions that accept either, so the two literals drive the same TRUE branch, and SPACES is the one a US-ASCII fixture carries as bytes rather than as escapes. The arm's statements then run in source order. :330 moves LIT-MENUTRANID, declared PIC X(4) VALUE 'CM00' at :170-171, into CDEMO-TO-TRANID, and :336 moves LIT-MENUPGM, PIC X(8) VALUE 'COMEN01C' at :168-169, into CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM - eight characters into a PIC X(08) receiver, so nothing is padded and nothing is truncated. :341-342 then record this screen as the from-pair, CAVW and COACTVWC, which is the swap this case pins alongside the fallback. :344 SET CDEMO-USRTYP-USER is unconditional and :345 SET CDEMO-PGM-ENTER rewinds the target's context to 0. :346 moves LIT-THISMAPSET, declared PIC X(8) VALUE 'COACTVW ', into CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET, which app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:43-44 declares PIC X(7) alongside CDEMO-LAST-MAP - so the alphanumeric MOVE truncates on the right and the literal's trailing space is deliberately discarded, giving COACTVW, while :347 moves the already-seven-character CACTVWA unchanged. The image compared here is that copybook's 160 bytes and no more: 4+8+4+8+8+1+1 = 34, then 9+25+25+25 = 84, then 11+1 = 12, then 16, then 7+7 = 14. Eight identity-bearing fields arrive populated and the arm clears none of them, so every one is expected back byte-identical: CDEMO-USER-ID is USER0001, a type-U row of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:40, and the other seven come from the seeded rows themselves - card 0500024453765740 keys customer 000000050 and account 00000000050 in cardxref row 1, whose account is acctdata row 50 and whose customer, names included, is custdata row 50. The inbound to-pair and last-pair still name this screen and the card list while the from-pair is blank, which is the state a client produces when it echoes the context back without repopulating the caller identity - precisely the state the two fallbacks exist for - and all four are overwritten by the arm regardless of what produced them. What this arm does NOT do is the rest of the expectation. XCTL at :349-352 transfers control and does not return, so :394 COMMON-RETURN is never reached, and 1000-SEND-MAP at :416 - with 1100-SCREEN-INIT at :431, 1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS at :460, 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS at :541 and 1400-SEND-SCREEN at :577 - never runs, and the :387-391 INPUT-ERROR guard is unreachable. Therefore: no map is painted, so sends is EMPTY and no title, TRNNAME, PGMNAME, date, time or 37-field projection appears anywhere in this expectation; expectedMessages is EMPTY rather than a list holding a blank line, because WS-RETURN-MSG was switched off at :278 and both the move into CCARD-ERROR-MSG at :395 and SEND-PLAIN-TEXT at :877 sit on paths not taken; nextMapset and nextMap are UNSET, because CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET and CCARD-NEXT-MAP are assigned only at :579-580 and at :603-604 and neither paragraph is performed; no cursor is positioned; 9000-READ-ACCT at :687 is never performed, so none of the three EXEC CICS READs at :727, :776 and :826 runs and all five seeded rows are pinned exactly as seeded, cardxref padded from its 36 fixture bytes to the 50 CVACT03Y declares (gate G16, risk R-F); and COACTVWC issues no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE on any path, so expectedWrites is empty and RETURN-CODE is 0, there being no CALL 'CEE3ABD' anywhere in this program (G35 not applicable, as are G32, G38 - no screen means no CSSETATY highlight - and G45/G47, since no read occurs). The clock is pinned at 2022-07-19T23:15:58 for determinism (practice B7) even though this path reads no clock at all. Every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by reading app/cbl/COACTVWC.cbl:278-352 with its WS-LITERALS at :143-171, app/cpy/CSSTRPFY.cpy:21-78, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44 and app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy, CVACT01Y.cpy and CVCUS01Y.cpy against the app/data/ASCII fixtures, and was NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution - the environment cannot run these programs (risk R-A), which is why the derivation is cited statement by statement here.
